title: Metastatic patterns in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck
summary:
Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma is one of the most common types of skin cancer and occurs particularly often in the head and neck region, especially in sun-exposed areas such as the lip or ear. The main cause is long-term exposure of the skin to sunlight. In some cases, the tumor spreads within the body, most commonly affecting lymph nodes in the neck and the parotid gland.
The aim of this study is to systematically investigate this spread. The study analyzes where the tumors originate, where they typically spread, and how frequently this occurs within the study population. In addition, it examines whether certain tumor-related or patient-related characteristics are associated with this process.
For this purpose, existing patient data from routine clinical care between January 2014 and December 2024 are analyzed. No additional examinations are performed. The data are analyzed in anonymized form.
The results may help to better understand the disease and improve treatment in the future.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm: Skin of other and unspecified parts of face

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck between January 2014 and December 2024 to investigate patterns of metastasis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck; diagnosis between January 2014 and December 2024; available staging data including documented N and/or M status
Exclusion criteria:
Non-cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma; primary tumors outside the head and neck region; missing histological confirmation; incomplete or non-evaluable data sets
